---
title: "Food Composition and Interaction Evidence"
format: html
execute:
  echo: true
---

This report examines nutrient co-occurrence in Kaggle food records and separates
it from the human-study interaction catalog. Run acquisition and analysis from
the RStudio project root before rendering. Food data are per 100 g.

```{r}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r}
manifest <- jsonlite::fromJSON("data-raw/kaggle-manifest.json")
manifest[c("title", "version", "license", "rows", "columns", "csv_md5")]
```

```{r}
read.csv("reports/generated/food-coverage.csv")
read.csv("reports/generated/food-correlations.csv", row.names = 1)
read.csv("reports/generated/food-pair-counts.csv", row.names = 1)
```

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("reports/generated/food-correlation.png")
```

The source spells iron `irom` and zinc `zink`; the cleaning script records their
mapping explicitly. Unit-bearing values are parsed strictly, with unitless zero
preserved. All five selected columns parse successfully. A reported zero may
reflect source reporting limits; absence of missing values does not establish
measurement completeness.

Correlations describe food records rather than individual intake or absorption.
Food group, water content and processing can confound the associations. These
records have no measured absorption outcomes, so absorption ML training and
predictive accuracy are unavailable in this increment.
